what_it_is: Space Kidz India is a Chennai-based organisation building student-led satellite missions, best known for the KalamSat series - including the 64-gram KalamSat, reported as the world's lightest satellite, flown via a NASA programme in 2017. It continues to design and launch small satellites built largely by school and college students.
india_angle: Space Kidz India is a uniquely Indian STEM-to-orbit pipeline: international coverage of its KalamSat missions (BBC among others) made student-built satellites a symbol of India's emerging private space culture, and its later missions ride Indian launch opportunities.
intelligence_assessment: Its mission record is verifiable through international media; institutional scale and technical depth should not be conflated with commercial space industry. Treat as an education-and-outreach player with genuine flight heritage.

faq.a: A 64-gram student-built pico-satellite by Space Kidz India, reported as the world's lightest satellite, flown in 2017 via a NASA initiative.
